premises.text: Development environments often do not match production environments, leading to wasted time chasing bugs.
premises.evidence_span: our development environments never matched up with our production environments. And what that means for us is that we end up going down rabbit holes, chasing bugs that we really didn't want to fix and really shouldn't have had to.

premises.text: Long testing times result in engineers being unproductive.
premises.evidence_span: Testing took forever. And when your tests take a long time to run, your engineers essentially are not doing work, and they end up sitting there, twiddling their thumbs, and just waiting for things to happen.

premises.text: Build breaks block the entire team from working and negatively impact morale.
premises.evidence_span: When a build break happens, your entire team is blocked from doing work, and your engineers end up raging.

premises.text: Quality can isolate changes to prevent build breaks and improve productivity.
premises.evidence_span: quality has just picked up the change. And what it actually does at this point is it takes that change and holds it in a limbo state.

premises.text: Quality can make development teams more effective by reducing testing times and build breaks.
premises.evidence_span: quality can make your development team 20% more effective.
